clue.text: Pass one side of the island

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
L for left, one side of anything

explanation.surface: Directions to get past an island by keeping to one side of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Coll is a small island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Coll is an island off the west coast of Scotland, an example of the category named.

definitions.meaning: a scornful idiom telling someone to stop talking nonsense
to get down off a horse or bike, to climb or fall away from it

explanation.surface: Someone scoffing at a rider while telling them to get down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a dismissive retort meaning stop the nonsense and a literal instruction to get down from a mount.

clue.text: Ale, it repeatedly upset the lady

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
repeatedly says the little word it is to be taken twice over

explanation.surface: Someone complains that beer keeps getting knocked over and the woman is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles IT to ITIT; with ALE that gives ALEITIT, which 'upset' rearranges into the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a woman's given name, so a particular lady.

definitions.meaning: having a fine tip, as a needle does
a fielding place in cricket, square of the batter on the off side

explanation.surface: A cricket captain sets a keen fielder in a sharp spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, point is a fielding position near the batter on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a tip is pointed, and point is also a named cricket fielding station.

parts.note: reads as performing a little, but means taking on a role or contributing to some undertaking

explanation.surface: An amateur dabbling briefly on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a role in something is literally to take a role in a play, and figuratively to contribute.

parts.note: sounds like scavenging the leftovers, but describes receiving what a dead person bequeathed

explanation.surface: Someone resignedly accepting the scraps after others have helped themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left to you in a will passes to you as an heir.

clue.text: Persuade European member to enter dry environment

indicators.note: to enter says these letters go into the word for dry
the dry word forms the surroundings that take the other letters in

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol
MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Coaxing a Euro politician into an alcohol-free setting.
explanation.walkthrough: TT (teetotal) is crossword shorthand for dry; MP is a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice someone is to persuade them by appealing to desire.

clue.text: You and I accepted one penny for sponge

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the pair word holds the other letters

parts.note: we covers you and me together
I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Two people take in a single penny in exchange for a bath sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge a surface is to clean it with a cloth, a synonym in verb sense.

parts.note: a river is a body of water
a ford is a shallow place for crossing a river

explanation.surface: A river crossing in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' looks like the river crossing the county, but it is FORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterford is a county in the south-east of the Republic of Ireland.

indicators.note: before places the stowing word ahead of the time word

parts.note: to pack something is to put it away in a case or box
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone stows a bundle before the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a bundle wrapped up together, a synonym.

clue.text: Meet asthmatic suffering about morning with logical analysis

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the morning letters
suffering means in a bad way, so the letters of these two words are disordered

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Meeting a wheezing patient one morning, with some careful reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' looks like the asthmatic's condition but signals the anagram; metamathematics is the branch of logic that studies mathematical proof itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Metamathematics studies the logical foundations and proofs of mathematics itself, a kind of formal reasoning.

indicators.note: remarkable suggests something out of the ordinary, so these letters are changed about

explanation.surface: Two people at an outstanding city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, an example of a city.

definitions.meaning: turning round and round, like a wheel on an axle
a member of an international service club for business people

explanation.surface: A radical political member of a gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a radical; it means rotary, turning round. Rotary International is a service club whose members bear this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Rotary Club carries this name, and the word also echoes rotary, meaning turning in circles.

clue.text: Father, a general, found it to be sweet-smelling

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
Ulysses S. Grant, Union general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A priest and an army general discover something with a lovely scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a pleasant scent is perfumed, a synonym.

parts.note: a guinea was twenty-one shillings, one pound and five pence in decimal money, so the clue imagines that coin as a creature

explanation.surface: A price tag asking whether a beast is worth one pound five.
explanation.walkthrough: The guinea, an old British gold coin, was worth 21 shillings, which is £1.05 in decimal money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavy, the small rodent kept as a pet, takes its name from the old coin worth this sum.

parts.note: suggests a child's spoon, but the nursery is a garden centre and the scoop is a hand tool for digging

explanation.surface: A spoon used at a children's playroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's small hand tool scoops out soil, as used at a plant nursery.

parts.note: describes refreshment shared between a pair, also the title of a famous song

explanation.surface: A remark about sharing a meal with company.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon cup and cake shared by a couple, the title of a popular song.

parts.note: the final trench a soldier could defend, the source of a phrase for a desperate final attempt

explanation.surface: The final stage of fighting from the trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate final effort is named after the last trench held in a battle.

clue.text: Half of this type of valley has sea-pink

indicators.note: half of says to take the first two of the four letters of the word this

parts.note: a rift valley is formed where the earth's crust pulls apart

explanation.surface: Half of this type of valley has a coastal flower growing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea-pink is another name for the coastal plant armeria, a synonym.

clue.text: German city's fast food unhesitatingly produced

definitions.note: the 's is read as is, so the definition is the city itself

indicators.note: without hesitation, so the er of hesitant speech is removed

parts.note: a burger in a bun, the classic fast food

explanation.surface: A German city's fast food is served up without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhesitatingly' removes ER, the sound of a speaker hesitating, from the end of the fast food.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamburg is a major port city in northern Germany.

clue.text: Ferns lad uprooted leaving poppy fields

indicators.note: uprooted means pulled out of place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy pulls up ferns as he walks away from a field of poppies.
explanation.walkthrough: The poppies of Flanders, in Belgium, became a symbol of the First World War dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanders is the Belgian region whose First World War battlefields bloomed with poppies.

indicators.note: about means around in a muddle, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A man worries about rising water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it rearranges HE FRETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshet is a sudden rise of a stream from rain or melting snow, a kind of flood.

parts.note: even as in even better, meaning still better
out means wrong, as a guess that is out

explanation.surface: A disappointed bookkeeper notes the accounts balance, yet the figures remain wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: When scores level off they become balanced, a phrasal synonym.

definitions.meaning: here a verb, to take something for one's own use
to steal money entrusted to one's care

explanation.surface: A suitable method of cheating someone out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as the adjective 'suitable'; it is the verb, to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To embezzle is to misappropriate funds held in trust, theft by an employee or trustee.

indicators.note: in a down entry, underneath puts the ring letter below the element

parts.note: zinc is a chemical element
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An element photographed with a ring beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A zinco is a print made from a zinc etching plate, so an illustration.

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
St is the abbreviation for street
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A ring road leading to an end point in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a port city on the Belgian coast, a place found there.

clue.text: Adam's apple, it indicates great emotion

definitions.meaning: the projection of cartilage at the front of the neck
the choked feeling felt when moved nearly to tears

explanation.surface: A remark on how a bulge in the neck signals deep feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam's apple is literally a bump in the neck, and the phrase also names the tight choked feeling of strong emotion.

clue.text: Keen part a go-go dancer has

indicators.note: part says only a portion of the following words is used
has means the dancer phrase contains the letters inside it

explanation.surface: An eager role taken on by a go-go dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eagerly excited is agog, a synonym.

definitions.meaning: a verb, to surpass or beat
a party held in the open air, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone excels at grilling outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits into OUT DO, a party (do) held outside, such as a barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass someone is to do more than them; split, the letters also make an open-air party.

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that a landlocked state has no port, at least in part.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the state is landlocked, so it is indeed without a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, an example of a state.
